title: A pause before the usual feed
description: Recall the chosen intention before the distraction, and let a suitable form of intervention be set up in advance.

blocks.text: Before a chosen distraction, a short pause and a reminder of the intention appear. The person decides whether they want to carry on. The point is a noticeable moment of choice, not a general ban on using the phone.

quote.text: I’m shocked at how just adding a forced pause before opening an app reduces my time on that app so much. The number of times I realize I don’t actually want to open the app but was just doing it out of habitual muscle memory is actually pretty wild.

blocks.text: The apps, the duration and the form of the intervention have to be set up separately. Vibration and sound can be removed; the work transitions you need should not trigger the same stop by accident. Real behavior is tested on the device.

It is worth looking not only at the number of pauses shown, but at whether they help a person reconsider an automatic open. If they mechanically wait for it to end every time, the scenario should be changed rather than the delay simply made longer.
